````text
# PR #3926: Patch: a banned account drops off the public Players list, as it already drops off the ranked leaderboard

Closes #3911

## What changed and why

When a player account is banned (`profiles.status = 'banned'`), its row was still visible in the public Players tab ranking and username search (`player_stats_list_public` in both Postgres and the in-memory fake store, and the public HTTP endpoint `GET /api/stats/players`). This patch extends [[R3290000]] to the public Players list (defined in new ruling note [[R3911000]]):

1. **Postgres query ([`pg.rs`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/src/db/pg.rs)):**
   In [`player_stats_list_public`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/src/db/pg.rs#L6790-L6815), added `and p.status <> 'banned'` to the `where` clause.
2. **Fake store ([`fake.rs`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/src/db/fake.rs)):**
   In [`player_stats_list_public`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/src/db/fake.rs#L3171-L3200), filtered out profiles where `p.status == ProfileStatus::Banned` when constructing `profile_map`.
3. **Spec and ruling documentation:**
   - Added ruling note [`R3911000.md`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/spec/rulings/R3911000.md).
   - Added pending §11 paragraph in [`3911.md`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/spec/pending/3911.md).
   - Cited `[[R3911000]]` in [`09-architecture.md`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/spec/09-architecture.md#L244) under §9.12 Public statistics and the publication gate.
4. **Contract and API tests:**
   - Added store contract test [`r3911000_list_public_excludes_banned_profile_and_restores_on_unban`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs#L3216-L3279) in `mod stats` inside [`contract.rs`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs), registered across both stores via `both_stores!`.
   - Added API test [`r3911000_get_api_stats_players_excludes_banned_profile_and_restores_when_unbanned`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs#L966-L1031) in [`stats.rs`](file:///home/agent-agy/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3911/crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs).

## Decisions and alternatives rejected

- **Filter at read-time vs delete on ban:** Modifying or deleting rows in `public.player_stats` upon account ban was rejected. The stored statistics are preserved intact so that lifting a ban (`moderate unban`) immediately restores the player's ranking and search appearance on the next read without requiring data recomputation or manual database edits.
````

````text
# #3911: Patch: a banned account drops off the public Players list, as it already drops off the ranked leaderboard
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The Statistics page has a public Players tab that ranks players by games played. Those numbers come from each player's own browser, so a cheater can send made-up totals and sit at the top. Banning is the moderators' tool, and a ban already takes an account off the ranked leaderboard. It does nothing to the Players tab, though: the banned account keeps its place until someone edits the database by hand. Once this is built, a banned account is left out of the Players tab and its search, and comes back when the ban is lifted.

## Why

- `player_stats_list_public` filters on privacy alone. In Postgres (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:6797-6808`) it reads `where ps.is_private = false`, ordered by games, most first. The in-memory store does the same (`crates/server/src/db/fake.rs:3171-3196`, `.filter(|r| !r.is_private)`).
- `GET /api/stats/players` needs no sign-in (`crates/server/src/app.rs:723`, `AuthLevel::None`).
- The counts are the client's (R1771000). `whole_count` (`crates/server/src/api/stats.rs:1544-1551`) accepts any whole number up to 2^53−1, so one hand-made `PUT /api/stats/player` puts an account at the top.
- `moderate ban` only sets `profiles.status` (`crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs:132-136`). That stops the account writing again, since an Active route refuses a banned profile (`crates/server/src/api/http.rs:811`), but the row stays public.
- R3290000 already keeps a banned account's standing off the public leaderboard, the percentiles and Jlorious (`pg.rs:5718`, `p.status = 'banned' as banned`; `fake.rs:3531`). The Players tab is the one public ranking it doesn't reach.

## Proposal

- The Postgres query adds `and p.status <> 'banned'`, and the in-memory store skips profiles whose status is `ProfileStatus::Banned`.
- A ruling note in the issue's block extends R3290000 to the Players tab, with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<N>.md`.
- Unbanning brings the row back. There is no migration, and the stored statistics are untouched.

## Where it lands

- `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`
- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, `crates/server/tests/api/stats.rs`
- `spec/rulings/`, `spec/pending/<N>.md`; SPEC §9.4, §9.12; R3290000, R1771000

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A store contract test, run on both stores: a banned profile with public statistics is absent from `player_stats_list_public`, with and without a search term, and is listed again once unbanned (fails today).
- [ ] An API test: `GET /api/stats/players` leaves the banned profile out.
- [ ] The ruling note lists its proving tests, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-server` passes, and `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` covers the Postgres query.

## Size and risks

Small: about 20 lines plus tests and a ruling. Nothing changes for players in good standing. A banned player's own stored copy is kept, so lifting the ban restores their row as it was.

   from public.player_stats ps
   join public.profiles p on p.id = ps.profile_id
   where ps.is_private = false
     and p.status <> 'banned'
     and ($1::text is null

   In `player_stats_list_public` (around line 3180), filter out banned profiles when generating `profile_map`:
   ```rust
   // Each profile's username as shown, and what a search reads of it.
   // R3911000: banned profiles drop off the public players list and its search.
   let profile_map: IndexMap<&str, (String, String)> = all
       .profiles
       .iter()
       .filter(|p| p.status != ProfileStatus::Banned)
       .map(|p| {
           let searched = match p.username_tag {
               Some(tag) => format!("{}#{tag}", p.username_key),
               None => p.username_key.clone(),
           };
           (p.id.as_str(), (p.username(), searched))
       })
       .collect();
   ```

       let p2 = active_profile(harness, None).await;

       for (profile, name) in [(&p1, "Alice_Banned"), (&p2, "Bob_Active")] {
           let claim = UsernameClaim {
               profile_id: profile.id.clone(),
               base: name.to_string(),
               key: username_key(name),
               expected_tag: None,
               at: now,
               cooldown_ms: USERNAME_CHANGE_COOLDOWN_MS,
           };
           q!(harness, t => t.profiles_claim_username(&claim));
       }

       let stats_1 = bag(json!({ "games": 200, "wins": 150, "losses": 50, "draws": 0 }));

       put_player_stats(&app, &alice_id, json!({ "games": 200, "wins": 150 }), false, 1000).await;
       put_player_stats(&app, &bob_id, json!({ "games": 100, "wins": 70 }), false, 2000).await;

       let (status, _, data) = get_public(&app, "/api/stats/players").await;
       assert_eq!(status, 200);
       let ids: Vec<&str> = data["players"]
           .as_array()
           .expect("players list")
           .iter()
           .map(|p| p["profileId"].as_str().unwrap_or_default())
           .collect();
       assert_eq!(ids, [alice_id.as_str(), bob_id.as_str()]);

       // Ban Alice
       {
           let mut tx = app.db.begin(Some(&alice_id)).await.expect("tx");
           tx.profiles_set_status(&alice_id, from(json!("banned")))
               .await
               .expect("set banned");
           tx.commit().await.expect("commit");
       }

       // Alice is excluded from /api/stats/players
       let (_, _, banned_data) = get_public(&app, "/api/stats/players").await;
       let banned_ids: Vec<&str> = banned_data["players"]
           .as_array()
           .expect("players list")
           .iter()
           .map(|p| p["profileId"].as_str().unwrap_or_default())
           .collect();
       assert_eq!(banned_ids, [bob_id.as_str()]);

       // Alice is excluded from search
       let (_, _, search_data) = get_public(&app, "/api/stats/players?search=Alice").await;
       assert_eq!(search_data["players"], json!([]));

       // Unban Alice
       {
           let mut tx = app.db.begin(Some(&alice_id)).await.expect("tx");
           tx.profiles_set_status(&alice_id, from(json!("active")))
               .await
               .expect("set active");
           tx.commit().await.expect("commit");
       }

       // Alice is restored
       let (_, _, restored_data) = get_public(&app, "/api/stats/players").await;
       let restored_ids: Vec<&str> = restored_data["players"]
           .as_array()
           .expect("players list")
           .iter()
           .map(|p| p["profileId"].as_str().unwrap_or_default())
           .collect();
       assert_eq!(restored_ids, [alice_id.as_str(), bob_id.as_str()]);
   }

## 6. Risks

- **Database Performance / Query Plan:** Adding `and p.status <> 'banned'` on `public.profiles` joined on `p.id = ps.profile_id`. `profiles.id` is the primary key. `profiles.status` has very few banned rows in practice. Joining by primary key and checking `p.status` does not alter index selection adversely on `player_stats`.
- **Data Loss / Permanence:** Unbanning an account must restore the previous statistics completely without requiring the user or moderators to re-upload. The change leaves `player_stats` table rows untouched; filtering is strictly query-time.
- **Store Drift:** Both `pg.rs` and `fake.rs` must agree precisely on sorting, filtering, and search behavior. This is guarded by running the identical test logic across both stores via `both_stores!`.
````
